question: In Canada, how can I tell from a package whether the whole food was irradiated or it just contains an irradiated ingredient?

The Regulations state that the label of a prepackaged irradiated food must carry the words "treated by irradiation" or "treated with irradiation" in close proximity to the food name or common name of the food on the principal display panel of the label. The purpose of food irradiation is to extend the shelf-life and to improve the microbiological safety of the food. 6. Is there a way for consumers to identify irradiated foods?
